title: With Compare or AI-led mode on, the PDF drawing is still uploaded to Anthropic while the screen says 'Read on this server — no AI, nothing leaves it'
module: CAD route (AI path) / CAD to COST screen
scenario: Code read: cad.ts:817, 1191-1212, 1276-1281, 1286-1306; parseAnalysisMode cad.ts:2410; main.ts:5842-5847, 5818; drawing-review.ts:22. The offline test (drawing-integration-offline.test.ts) runs with AIR_GAPPED=1 and so cannot exercise this path.
expected: Brief §3: drawings are never uploaded to external servers. At minimum, the screen's offline claim matches what happens, or the drawing is withheld from the model.
actual: drawingForModel = any upload whose first 1 KB contains %PDF- (cad.ts:817). It is base64-sent to the Stage-1 vision call (cad.ts:1206, stage1Identify→identifyPart) and attached as a 'document' block to the specialist prompt (cad.ts:1276-1281, sent by cadAnalyzeJSON on the AI path). This happens when (a) mode='ai' or 'both' (the 'AI-led (legacy)' / 'Compare — rules vs AI' options in More options, main.ts:5842-5847, shown when a key exists), with a key and AIR_GAPPED unset; or (b) an API caller omits `mode`, the commodity has no rule pack and the server holds a key (fallback, cad.ts:1286-1306). Image/DXF drawings are never sent. The static line DRAWING_OFFLINE_LINE ('Read on this server — no AI, nothing leaves it', drawing-review.ts:22) is printed on the attach row (main.ts:5818) and the review panel (drawing-review.ts:401) in every mode. The feature doc (docs/cad/offline-drawing-intelligence-2026-11.md §3 'AI off or on') does not mention the upload.
evidence: Code read: cad.ts:817, 1191-1212, 1276-1281, 1286-1306; parseAnalysisMode cad.ts:2410; main.ts:5842-5847, 5818; drawing-review.ts:22. The offline test (drawing-integration-offline.test.ts) runs with AIR_GAPPED=1 and so cannot exercise this path.
rootCause: The pre-existing AI drawing path was kept 'exactly as before' and only narrowed to PDFs; the new offline claim was written as an unconditional UI string.
recommendedAction: Never pass the drawing to the model (drop drawingForModel), or require an explicit per-request opt-in and change the UI text to say the drawing is sent when AI mode is on; refuse the no-mode AI fallback when a drawing is attached; add a test with AI mode on, a fake key and blocked sockets asserting zero outbound attempts with a drawing attached.
retest: tests/drawing-validation-fixes.test.ts F01/F02: no drawing document in any model request; model drawing reads stripped

title: In AI mode, a second, unconfirmed drawing reading (the model's) reaches the cost beside the offline review
module: CAD to COST screen / AI number guard
scenario: Code read: main.ts:14166-14240; server/utils/ai-number-guard.ts:41-51; cad.ts:1454 (drawingGearRead feeds the sanity check).
expected: Brief §4 L3 and §12: one unified dataset; only engineer-validated drawing values reach the costing.
actual: When service.finish is not answered, the screen reads costInputSuggestions.surfaceTreatment written by the model from the PDF: the callout sets the finish route select (main.ts:14196-14207), and thickness / masked features are written into -sf-um / -sf-mask after boundDrawingCoating (main.ts:14217-14226). ai-number-guard.ts:41-51 keeps surfaceTreatment.thicknessUm / maskedFeatureCount and the gear drawing reads (helix, quality class, case depth held as pre-selected leanings via withAIGearAnswers). None of these is a parameter in Layer 3, none appears in the review panel, none needs a confirm, and they can disagree with the offline reading of the same sheet with no conflict raised. The screen path has no headless twin, so screen ≠ headless with a drawing in AI mode.
evidence: Code read: main.ts:14166-14240; server/utils/ai-number-guard.ts:41-51; cad.ts:1454 (drawingGearRead feeds the sanity check).
rootCause: The legacy AI drawing path (coating-drawing-read.ts, drawingGearRead, surfaceTreatment) was not routed through the unified layer.
recommendedAction: With a drawing attached, ignore the model's surfaceTreatment / gear drawing reads (or feed them into consolidate() as a third source with status needs-validation) so the review panel is the only path from a drawing to a cost.
retest: same test: stripModelDrawingReads drops finish and gear drawing fields

title: Values worked out from an OCR reading are marked 'extracted' (no doubt) while their OCR source stays 'needs-validation'
scenario: Probe scratchpad/validation/audit/probes/probe4.ts output: 'drawing:material.designation:1>material.grade "mat-gjs500" extracted rule 0.41' … 'answers with OCR origins unconfirmed: {"material.family":"cast iron","material.grade":"mat-gjs500","service.toleranceClass":"tight"}'.
expected: Brief §8: OCR / uncertain readings are flagged for review. A value derived from an unconfirmed OCR reading should not show the 'Read' (successfully extracted) status.
actual: derive() defaults status to 'extracted' whatever the origin's status. Probe: OCR 'EN-GJS-500-7' at reliability 0.41 (needs-validation) → material.grade 'mat-gjs500' and material.family 'cast iron' both status 'extracted'. Confirming only the two derived rows (origin left unconfirmed) gives answers {material.family: cast iron, material.grade: mat-gjs500} and the origin is still needs-validation. 'Confirm all read exactly' does walk the chain (present.ts:136-145) and excludes these, so the leak needs a per-row click, but the status word shown on the row is wrong.
evidence: Probe scratchpad/validation/audit/probes/probe4.ts output: 'drawing:material.designation:1>material.grade "mat-gjs500" extracted rule 0.41' … 'answers with OCR origins unconfirmed: {"material.family":"cast iron","material.grade":"mat-gjs500","service.toleranceClass":"tight"}'.
rootCause: derive() does not inherit needs-validation from an OCR / needs-validation origin.
recommendedAction: Make derive() take the worse of the rule's status and the origin's status (needs-validation whenever the origin is), or require the origin to be confirmed before a derived value is usable in the adapter.
retest: drawing-validation-fixes F03: OCR-derived values are needs-validation

title: A saved review is replayed by parameter id only; a reader change can make a 'confirm' land on a different reading
scenario: Code read: index.ts:240-250; review-state.ts:84-85, 406-437; drawing-review-ui.ts:263-295. Not reproduced (READER_VERSION is 1.0.0 everywhere today).
expected: Brief §4 'Record manual corrections and overrides' / §15.12 saved data stays valid: a decision applies to the value the engineer saw, or is skipped.
actual: Reader ids are ordinal per name (`drawing:${name}:${n}`, index.ts:248). A confirm / reject / reopen op carries only the id (review-state.ts:84-85), never the value it confirmed. restoreSavedReview (drawing-review-ui.ts:277-295) replays saved ops whenever the drawing hash matches; the saved readerVersion (drawing-review-ui.ts:271) is never compared with the current one, and the server re-reads under a new READER_VERSION (cache key). After an extractor change re-orders readings of one name, a stored confirm silently confirms whichever reading now holds that ordinal, and the restore immediately re-runs the costing with it (hooks.rerun).
evidence: Code read: index.ts:240-250; review-state.ts:84-85, 406-437; drawing-review-ui.ts:263-295. Not reproduced (READER_VERSION is 1.0.0 everywhere today).
rootCause: Decisions are keyed on unstable positional ids and carry no value fingerprint.
recommendedAction: Store the confirmed value (or a hash of name+rawText+location) in every op and skip the op when it no longer matches; refuse or flag a restore whose readerVersion differs.
retest: drawing-review-binding.test.ts (12): decisions bound to drawing hash and seen value

title: Override history 'by' and 'at' are whatever the client sends — not the authenticated user
scenario: Code read: review-state.ts:72-80; cad.ts:1101; drawing-context.ts:79-85; main.ts:6799-6805.
expected: Brief §4 provenance: user override history. The server should stamp who decided from the session.
actual: parseReviewState takes `by` from the request (default 'engineer') and `at` from the request; cad.ts:1101 and drawing-context.ts:84 pass it straight to replay. The screen fills `by` from localStorage auth_user display name (main.ts installDrawingReviewHooks `who`). Any caller can write any name and time into the history that the reports print.
evidence: Code read: review-state.ts:72-80; cad.ts:1101; drawing-context.ts:79-85; main.ts:6799-6805.
rootCause: Decisions are designed to be replayable client data; the identity was not bound to req.user.
recommendedAction: Overwrite `by` with req.user (id + name) on the server for ops not already stored, or store ops server-side per user and replay only those.
retest: drawing-review-binding / drawing-integration-routes: server stamps who and when

title: Drawings, readings, sheet pictures and OCR jobs are not scoped to the user who uploaded them
scenario: Code read: drawing.ts:73-100; drawing-service.ts:264-278, 314-332; drawing-context.ts:79-85.
expected: Confidential drawings readable only by the uploader (or their organisation).
actual: GET /api/drawing/:hash/sheet/:n and GET /api/drawing/jobs/:id?reading=1 (full extraction text) need only any valid session; getDrawing / getSheetImage / getDrawingJob take no user. /reanalyze, compare-routes and option-costs accept any drawingHash and return the full engineeringData. The extraction cache is global (one row per SHA-256). Exposure requires knowing the hash (possession of the file) or the job UUID, so the practical risk is limited, but there is no per-user check at all.
rootCause: The drawing store was modelled on the global geometry cache.
recommendedAction: Record the uploading user (or org) with each drawing / job and check it on every read; return 404 otherwise.
retest: drawing-access-scope.test.ts (7): two users and an admin

title: Drawing files and readings outlive their stated retention on a long-running server
scenario: Code read: drawing.ts:26; drawing-service.ts:96-123; server/utils/analysis-cache.ts:21-47.
expected: Doc §9: files kept a day, readings a week.
actual: sweepDrawingFiles runs once when routes/drawing.ts is imported (drawing.ts:26); expired files are otherwise deleted only when the same hash is read again (getDrawingBytes, drawing-service.ts:107). Sheet PNGs are only swept by that start-up sweep. The SQLite extraction cache (all drawing text) is purged on start-up and on access (analysis-cache.ts:30,47). A drawing nobody re-opens stays in os.tmpdir()/cv-drawing-files and in SQLite until the next restart.
rootCause: Retention is enforced lazily.
recommendedAction: Run the sweep on an interval (unref'd timer) for files, sheet PNGs and the extraction table; document the location in the deployment notes.
retest: drawing-access-scope: hourly sweeper

title: Image and TIFF drawings are decoded at full resolution before any pixel cap (decompression-bomb risk)
scenario: Code read: render.ts:11-12, 69-106; worker.ts:207-226. Not reproduced.
expected: Resource limits: a 30 MB upload cannot exhaust a 2 GB VM.
actual: decodeBitmap calls loadImage (full decode) before computing the MAX_PIXELS shrink (render.ts:69-83). decodeTiff decodes every page with UTIF.decodeImage + toRGBA8 and keeps all pages' grey buffers, with no pixel limit at all (render.ts:87-106). A highly compressed CCITT/LZW TIFF or PNG of very large dimensions fits in 30 MB and expands to many GB of native memory inside a worker thread of the server process (Worker has no resourceLimits; worker.ts:214-217).
evidence: Code read: render.ts:11-12, 69-106; worker.ts:207-226. Not reproduced.
rootCause: The pixel cap is applied after decoding and not at all for TIFF.
recommendedAction: Read width × height from the header (PNG IHDR, JPEG SOF, TIFF IFD tags 256/257) and refuse or downsample before decoding; decode TIFF pages one at a time; give the worker resourceLimits or run OCR in a child process.
retest: drawing-raster-limits.test.ts (14): 150 MP cap before decode, PNG row-wise; JPEG still decodes full size under the cap

title: 'AlSi7Mg0.3' (A356 / LM25) is offered only A357 (AlSi7Mg0.6) as its grade candidate
scenario: Probe scratchpad/validation/audit/probes/probe3.ts: 'AlSi7Mg0.3 mat-a357 needs-validation [{"value":"mat-a357","label":"A357 / AlSi7Mg0.6 (Premium T6)"}]'. rate-library.ts:535 (mat-lm25 'LM25 / A356'), :594 (mat-a357).
expected: A designation is matched to the right rate-book grade, or none; candidates include the correct grade.
actual: On casting / cast_and_machine, 'AlSi7Mg0.3' → material.grade 'mat-a357' (needs-validation) with candidates [A357 / AlSi7Mg0.6]; the library grade 'mat-lm25' (LM25 / A356) is not offered. The status is needs-validation, so it is not used without a click, but the single candidate the panel offers is the wrong alloy (A357 £3.20/kg). 'EN AC-42100' (the EN number for the same alloy) resolves to nothing.
evidence: Probe scratchpad/validation/audit/probes/probe3.ts: 'AlSi7Mg0.3 mat-a357 needs-validation [{"value":"mat-a357","label":"A357 / AlSi7Mg0.6 (Premium T6)"}]'. rate-library.ts:535 (mat-lm25 'LM25 / A356'), :594 (mat-a357).
rootCause: The shared-stem matcher (gradeEvidence) truncates at 'AlSi7Mg' and the Mg content suffix is ignored.
recommendedAction: Treat the Mg suffix (0.3 v 0.6) as distinguishing, add EN AC numbers / A356 aliases, and always list every same-stem grade as a candidate.
retest: drawing-validation-fixes F09: EN 1706 designations

title: On machining, a drawing grade (e.g. 42CrMo4) only answers the family; the grade itself is neither costed nor listed as 'not costed'
scenario: Probe probe2.ts: 'replay on machining … answers {} notCosted []' and per-commodity table '42CrMo4 machining: material.family=steel'.
expected: Brief §12 traceability: what the drawing specifies and the cost does not use is said.
actual: MACHINING_PACK binds material.family only. The designation is 'consumed' through its family, so computeNotCosted (reconcile.ts:379-403) does not list it; the panel and the reports show the material as used, while machining costs the family's representative bar, not 42CrMo4. Same for forging of an alloy not offered on that route, and for casting/forging grades outside the route's grade list (they become 'missing' notes, not 'not costed').
evidence: Probe probe2.ts: 'replay on machining … answers {} notCosted []' and per-commodity table '42CrMo4 machining: material.family=steel'.
rootCause: 'Consumed' is decided by name, not by whether the whole value reached a question.
recommendedAction: When only the family of a designation is used, add a not-costed entry 'grade 42CrMo4 — this route costs the family's representative grade'.
retest: drawing-validation-fixes F10: grade listed as not costed on machining

title: ISO 2768-m (the default title-block note) maps to tolerance class 'tight', which on ferrous castings means investment casting
scenario: Code read: interpret-tables.ts:62-101; service-context.ts:76-93. Probe4: 'ISO 2768-mK' → tolerance.generalClass 'tight'.
expected: A general machining tolerance should not, once confirmed, move a cast part to investment casting.
actual: iso2768-letter rule: f and m → 'tight'; the 'tight' option's consequence is 'investment casting or added machining' (service-context.ts:84-88). The rule's own basis says ISO 2768-1 governs machined features, not the as-cast tolerance. It is certainty 'judgement' → needs-validation, so it needs a click, but the interpretation the panel proposes is a large cost lever on castings and forgings. The DCTG bands are also unsourced ('the annex was not re-read in this build').
evidence: Code read: interpret-tables.ts:62-101; service-context.ts:76-93. Probe4: 'ISO 2768-mK' → tolerance.generalClass 'tight'.
rootCause: One tolerance-class question serves both machined and as-cast tolerances.
recommendedAction: On casting / forging routes do not interpret ISO 2768 into the as-cast tolerance class (leave it 'not readable into this question'); source the DCTG bands.
retest: engineering-data-interpret: ISO 2768 / DIN 7168 answer no as-cast class

title: GD&T characteristics are not recognised on the public vector drawing documented as using the AIGDT symbol font

evidence: npx tsx server/drawing/cli.ts tests/fixtures/drawings/nist-ftc-07.pdf --json → 20 frames, characteristic null; docs/cad/offline-drawing-intelligence-2026-11.md §5.

title: Hole-and-boss count for the mask cap is computed in three places
scenario: grep output above.
expected: One helper.
actual: measuredMaskable (drawing-context.ts:132-135), main.ts:6812-6815 (hooks.measuredMaskable) and main.ts:14222 each sum featureTable hole/boss counts; to-costing.ts:363-364 has a fourth fallback from feature.count.holes (holes only). The screen preview and the server could cap differently if one copy changes.

title: A confirmed drawing family silently outranks the family read from the CAD file name; no conflict row
expected: Brief §4: never silently overwrite one source with another.
actual: answersFromContext(forcedMaterial, filename) turns a family word in the file name into an ANSWER (cad.ts:2178-2192). That evidence is not a Layer-3 parameter (from-cad.ts maps only cadMetadata), so a confirmed drawing family that differs (file 'Aluminium_bracket.stp', drawing 'S355') is applied over it by withDrawingAnswers with no conflict shown. Documented as intended ('a name is a prior').
rootCause: Name evidence lives outside the unified layer.
recommendedAction: Map the file-name family into consolidate() as source 'name' so a disagreement is shown as a conflict with the precedence suggestion.
retest: File-name family is not a conflict source

title: Client-supplied drawingFile name replaces the source file recorded on every parameter
scenario: Code read.
expected: Source file is the uploaded file's name.
actual: drawingFromBody passes body.drawingFile to getDrawing, and recordOf rewrites sourceFile on every parameter with it (drawing-service.ts:154). Reports print this name.
rootCause: Same bytes under another name are treated as the same drawing, and the request's name is trusted.
recommendedAction: Keep the name recorded at upload as sourceFile; show the request's name only as a label.
retest: Client-supplied drawingFile name can relabel the source file

title: engineering-data-packs test times out under parallel load

scenario: Code read: to-costing.ts:21,123; interpret.ts:23,105.

title: The word GEOMETRIC is read as the zinc-flake trade name GEOMET: a note about geometric tolerances becomes an exact-text coating reading that "Confirm all read exactly" applies
scenario: B18 / B18b / B18c; A15 (NIST CTC-02)
expected: A note such as "GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES TO ISO 1101." produces no coating reading; the finish question stays as it is without a drawing
actual: finish.coating = "GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES TO ISO 1101." and finish.coatingRoute = zinc_flake, both status 'extracted' (exact text, no needs-checking flag). On a steel cast + machine costing it is a leaning on service.finish, so it is in the "Confirm all read exactly" set; one confirm answers service.finish = zinc_flake and the headless cost moves from £10.1696 to £10.5526 (+3.8 %). On the public NIST CTC-02 sheet five sentences that mention "geometric tolerances" became finish.coating readings and a zinc-flake route, all 'extracted'.
rootCause: server/drawing/extract/coating.ts:12 — the zinc-flake pattern is /\b(?:DACROMET|GEOMET(?:\s?\d{3})?|…)/i with no trailing word boundary, so it matches the start of GEOMETRIC/GEOMETRY. src/engine/engineering-data/interpret-tables.ts:148 has the same problem (/…|geomet|…/i, no boundaries).
recommendedAction: Add a trailing word boundary (GEOMET\b, also for the other trade names) in both tables; add a regression test with the notes "GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES TO ISO 1101", "GEOMETRY" and the NIST CTC-02 sheet; consider marking trade-name-only coating readings needs-validation.
retest: drawing-validation-fixes D01: GEOMETRIC/GEOMETRY read no coating

title: A review made on one drawing is replayed onto a different drawing: positional reading ids match a different reading with a different value
expected: Per the design doc, a decision that no longer applies is skipped and listed, never matched to another reading. A review made on real-casting-bracket.pdf (confirming material family = aluminium) must not confirm anything on another drawing.
actual: Sending the bracket's review with the GEAR drawing (via /analyze with that drawing, or /reanalyze naming the gear drawing's hash) applied 'confirm drawing:material.designation:1>material.family' to the gear drawing's reading, whose value is steel (20MnCr5): drawingCosting.answers = {"material.family":"steel"} on the bracket costing. 8 of 10 ops were skipped, 2 applied to different values.
rootCause: Reading ids are positional ("drawing:<parameter>:<n>") and ReviewOp carries neither the drawing hash nor the value that was confirmed (review-state.ts:18-27); replayReview applies any op whose id exists in the new dataset. The screen guards this by resetting the review when the drawing hash changes (src/ui/drawing-review-ui.ts:186-187), but the server accepts any review with any drawing. The same mechanism would apply a stored review to a re-read made by a newer reader version if the reading order changes.
recommendedAction: Stamp each op (or the review) with the drawing hash and reader version and the value seen when the decision was taken; on replay skip an op whose reading's value differs, and refuse/skip a review made for another hash.
retest: drawing-review-replay-route.test.ts: a review on another drawing is skipped

title: Core PDF and workbook say "no drawing is read" on a costing that has a drawing read and applied
scenario: D — casting bracket and gear with drawing
expected: With a drawing attached, the DFM 'not checked' line does not claim that no drawing is read
actual: Core PDF §7 (page 8 casting, page 6 gear) and workbook 0-Executive!A235: "Not checked: tolerances, datums and finish call-outs (no drawing is read)." — the same report prints the drawing specification table and the stamp naming the drawing reader.
rootCause: src/export/executive-summary.ts:1342 — the notChecked sentence is a constant written before the drawing reader existed.
recommendedAction: When a drawing is attached, say what the reader does and does not check (e.g. tolerances read but not costed; GD&T symbols drawn as geometry not read).
retest: report-reliability-fixes: drawing-aware wording

title: Audit pack §1: the reproducibility stamp runs off the right edge of the page when a drawing is attached
scenario: D — audit pack, casting bracket and gear with drawing
expected: The stamp is printed in full (it is meant to be quoted word for word)
actual: Page 4: "… drawing reader v1.0.0 · real-casting-bracket.pdf 6f1a98cf · 10 Nov 202" (clipped); gear: "… gear-drawing-WRONG-z40.pdf c58b93dd · 10" (date clipped). Without a drawing the line fits.
rootCause: src/export/pdf.ts:1032 — doc.text(`Reproducibility: ${cadMeta.stamp}`, MG, y + 1) with no maxWidth / splitTextToSize; the drawing suffix makes the line wider than the content width.
recommendedAction: Wrap the line (splitTextToSize to CW) and advance y by the wrapped height.
retest: report-reliability-fixes: stamp wraps

title: PDF drops the thread-depth symbol: "M6x1-6H ↧ 12" prints as "M6x1-6H  12"
scenario: D — audit pack §9c (casting bracket)
expected: The value reads as on the drawing / workbook (M6x1-6H ↧ 12) or with a word ("depth 12")
actual: Audit pack page 22 prints "M6x1-6H  12" (blank where ↧ was); workbook 10-Drawing prints "M6x1-6H ↧ 12". "M6x1-6H 12" can be read as a thread length.
rootCause: src/export/pdf.ts:434 (winAnsiSafe) strips every character outside WinAnsi; U+21A7 has no replacement mapping (Ø, ±, ° and µ survive).
recommendedAction: Map ↧ to "depth" (and ⌴ / ⌵ to "counterbore" / "countersink") in winAnsiSafe before the strip.
retest: report-reliability-fixes: drawing symbols as words in the PDF

title: Two confidence grades for one costing: screen, core PDF and 0-Executive say Medium; audit pack and 1-Summary say Low
scenario: D — all three costings (also with NO drawing)
expected: One grade everywhere (CLAUDE.md: 'one confidence grade')
actual: Casting bracket: screen 'Band · confidence Medium', core PDF p1 'Medium confidence', 0-Executive!A41 'Medium'; audit pack cover 'Model Confidence: Low', executive summary 'CONFIDENCE Low', §7 'Why confidence is Low'; workbook 1-Summary!A24 'Model confidence Low'. Same on both gear costings (with and without drawing).
rootCause: Core grades the DISTINCT inputs (executive-summary.ts:961 gradeOfCounts: 12 inputs, 0 High / 11 Medium / 1 Low → Medium); the audit pack cover / workbook summary grade every data point with overallConfidence(result) (pdf.ts ~2693: 27 points, 0 / 21 / 6 → Low). Not caused by the drawing feature.
recommendedAction: Use one grading function and one input population for every surface; add a test that screen, core, audit and workbook grades are equal.
retest: report-reliability-fixes + casting-360-review: one grade (costingConfidence) on screen, PDF, workbook

title: 30 MB exactly: /api/drawing/read refuses it (413) while /api/cad/analyze accepts it
scenario: A13b
expected: The same limit on both routes (the doc: 'Limit 30 MB')
actual: A 31,457,280-byte PDF: /api/drawing/read → 413 'The drawing is over the 30 MB limit.'; /api/cad/analyze → 200, drawing ready. 30 MB + 1 byte is refused by both.
rootCause: server/routes/drawing.ts:28 sets multer limits.fileSize = MAX_DRAWING_BYTES and busboy fires 'limit' when the size REACHES the limit (node_modules/busboy/lib/types/multipart.js:476 fileSize === fileSizeLimit); cad.ts:805 tests size > MAX_DRAWING_PDF_BYTES.
recommendedAction: Set the multer limit to MAX_DRAWING_BYTES + 1 and check size > MAX in the route, as cad.ts does.
retest: drawing-access-scope: exactly 30 MB accepted on both routes

title: Over-limit message rounds the size: "Drawing is 30 MB; the limit is 30 MB."
scenario: A14 (30 MB + 1 byte on /api/cad/analyze)
expected: A message that shows why the file was refused
actual: HTTP 413 'Drawing is 30 MB; the limit is 30 MB.'
rootCause: server/routes/cad.ts:806 — (size / 1048576).toFixed(0).
recommendedAction: Print one decimal (as server/drawing/ingest.ts checkSize does) or say 'over'.
retest: 413 message states bytes and the limit

title: A scan turned 90° is reported as read upright but yields a wrong material (S310N → steel) for an aluminium A356-T6 drawing
scenario: A16c
expected: The sheet is turned upright before OCR (as a vector PDF with /Rotate is) or the reading says it could not be read reliably
actual: casting-bracket-rot90.png: warning 'the drawing is turned 90° on its page; it was read upright', 52 words at 72 % mean confidence, 3 readings: material.designation 'S310N', material.family 'steel', one dimension. The same sheet upright reads 37 readings incl. A356-T6 / aluminium. All three are needs-validation, so nothing is costed until confirmed.
rootCause: Observed behaviour only; raster/index.ts OCRs the image as given and again after rotate90cw for vertical words (lines 81-121) rather than choosing the page orientation first. Not traced further.
recommendedAction: Detect the page orientation (0/90/180/270) on the whole scan and OCR once in the best orientation; warn when mean confidence is low.
retest: drawing-raster-limits: four-turn orientation probe (A16c reads A356-T6)

title: Rotation is reported inconsistently: sheet.rotationDeg and the warning disagree
expected: One rotation figure per sheet
actual: Vector PDF with /Rotate 90: sheets[0].rotationDeg = 90, warning 'the drawing is turned 270° on its page'. Raster turned 90°: rotationDeg = 0, warning 'turned 90°'.
rootCause: rotationDeg is the PDF page /Rotate (pdf-vector.ts:194; raster sheets hard-code 0 at index.ts:150) while the warning prints the dominant text rotation q (index.ts:220-228).
recommendedAction: Report both under distinct names, or report the text rotation in rotationDeg.
retest: one rotation convention in stats and warning

title: OCR structural mis-assignments on skewed / low-resolution scans (wrong title-block cells, Ø read as 9, decimal point lost)
expected: Readings that are wrong are absent or flagged; key cells land in the right field
actual: Skew 3°: title.partNumber = 'CASTING BRACKET', title.scale = 'ISO 8062-3 DCTG 6'. Skew 7°: tolerance.general = 'ISO 2768-mK' (the machined-dimension note) instead of DCTG 6. 200 dpi upright: '4× Ø13' read as dimension 913 (×4). 72 dpi: roughness 'Ra 63' (6.3), dimensions 1081 / 122 / 112. Every one is status needs-validation (as documented) and none is confirmed by 'Confirm all read exactly'.
rootCause: Documented OCR limits (doc §5, §9); not traced in code.
recommendedAction: Warn on low resolution (< 150 dpi) and reject title-block values that do not fit their cell (a scale must look like n:m).
retest: OCR mis-assignments on skewed / 72 dpi scans; all flagged needs-validation

title: Server memory after OCR reads: node RSS grows to ~1.1-1.2 GB and stays; peak 2.0 GB (node + geometry worker) on an A0 image
expected: The OCR pass fits the 2 GB VM (doc §3: one at a time because the VM has 2 GB)
actual: Process-group RSS sampled every 150 ms: idle 400-607 MB; A0 300 dpi PNG (14039×9928) read peak 2,019 MB; during the 9-image queue the node process alone was 1,173 MB with the geometry worker at 304 MB; after the run node stayed at 1,104 MB (+2 geometry workers 351 + 349 MB = 1,823 MB group).
rootCause: Not traced; RSS is not returned after the OCR passes (WebAssembly / worker heap). Measured on a 16 GB host, so no OOM was seen.
recommendedAction: Measure in the 2 GB Docker image; cap the OCR image size; terminate the OCR worker after each pass so its memory is returned.
retest: reader peak 910 → 433 MB on the A0 scan; whole server group not re-measured; worker has no resourceLimits

title: Core page 1 says the CAD model shows no thread while the confirmed drawing on the same report states M6x1-6H
scenario: D — casting bracket core PDF
expected: With a drawing that states a thread, the 'Not included until answered' item says the drawing states one (not costed)
actual: Page 1: 'Threads not detected — confirm: the CAD model shows no thread … say which holes are tapped and their size'; page 3 lists Thread among the drawing's not-costed readings (M6x1-6H ↧ 12).
rootCause: Not traced.
recommendedAction: When the drawing states threads, name them in that line.
retest: report-reliability-fixes: threads stated on the drawing are named

title: Audit pack §9b heading: the subtitle overlaps the title
scenario: D — casting bracket audit pack page 18
expected: Title and subtitle separate
actual: '§9b — Route Comparison' is overprinted by 'the same part on every route and process that can make it in its material · reference: Cast and machine — gravity die casting'. Not seen on the gear (shorter subtitle). Not caused by the drawing feature.

recommendedAction: Shorten or wrap the subtitle when it would reach the title.
retest: report-reliability-fixes: §9b subtitle wraps

title: DXF reader joins the next note's number to a note and does not read a 'PART No.' text
expected: 'PRESSURE TEST AT 6 bar'; part number CB-2207-11
actual: quality.leakTestSpec = 'PRESSURE TEST AT 6 bar 2.' (the next TEXT's '2.' appended); no title.partNumber from 'PART No. CB-2207-11'. 3 of 6 key readings (material, tolerance, leak, coating found; designation read as EN AC-42100, which is the same alloy).
rootCause: Not traced. The test DXF is hand-made (TEXT entities, no title-block table), so this is indicative.
recommendedAction: Check line assembly for DXF TEXT that starts with a note number.
retest: DXF note numbering appended to the leak-test text

title: Review cache key includes each decision's timestamp and author
expected: The doc: 'the same decisions give the same text, for cache keys'
actual: reviewStateKey of the same confirm with at 09:00 v 09:05 differs (scripts/keycheck.mts: equal false). Over HTTP (B08) answers and cost were identical; the deterministic /analyze path is never cached, so the key difference only matters on the cached (AI) paths, where a different key means a new model call.
rootCause: review-state.ts:124-130 serialises the whole op including by / at / reason.
recommendedAction: Key on op, id/name and value only; keep by/at for the record.
retest: drawing-review-binding: review key depends on decisions only

title: Drawings whose annotation is stroke-font polylines (NIST D2MI, Siemens NX) are classed as vector text: no OCR runs, nothing is read, and no warning says so
scenario: Read the six NIST D2MI drawings (827-9999-903..908), alone (read-one.mts) and attached to their STEP on /api/cad/analyze
expected: Sheets classed text-as-curves (or mixed) and OCR'd; failing that, a warning that the annotation was not read
actual: Every sheet 'vector-text' (3 text runs: the NX plot stamp 'Scale= 0.5000:1', '20150310.1524 [NX8] File: …', 'tamatusk'); 0 parameters; warnings []; ocrWouldRead false so the server never queues OCR. 350 truth items (title block, 6061-T6/T651 material, ASTM standard, chromate conversion coating, dimensions, GD&T) - 0 found. The engineer sees a drawing with no readings and no reason.
evidence: runs/raw/nist-d2mi-90{3..8}.json; runs/scripts/sheet-stats.mts output: {pathOps:2968, glyphLikePaths:0, imageCoverage:0, textChars:67, textItems:3} -> classify 'vector-text'; runs/reconciliation.json pair:nist-d2mi-904 / 906 (FAIL)
rootCause: server/drawing/ingest.ts:88 — textChars >= 25 (the plot stamp alone) returns 'vector-text' unless glyphLikePaths >= 20; stroke-font text is short line segments, not glyph-sized closed outlines, so glyphLikePaths = 0 although pathOps = 2,968. isMixedSheet (ingest.ts:104-106) needs glyphLikePaths >= 20 too, so no 'partly curves' warning and ocrWouldRead (index.ts:46-50) is false.
retest: stroke-font sheets now OCR'd: D2MI recall 0 → 10 %, but 139 wrong (all needs-validation) — see M-D16

title: Scanned sheets carrying a scanner OCR text layer are read as EXACT text when the page has more than 20 path operators
scenario: NTRS Stirling report pages 159, 161, 163, 170 (full-page image + invisible scanner OCR layer + 28-120 path ops); also on the original 359-page report pages
expected: Classed 'scanned', the scanner layer ignored (index.ts:114 already does this when detected) and the page OCR'd by the reader with 'needs validation' readings
actual: Classed 'vector-text'; scanner OCR garbage becomes method 'pdf-text', reliability 1, status 'extracted' (shown as exact text): thread 'M1' from 'M1 I.JlL-6a', dimensions 80020 from '80020~', 611 from '0611_..-', nominal 0 from '0 -' and '00'. Pages 172 / 200 (pathOps 0 / 11) are handled correctly. None of these readings answers a costing question, so no £ moved, but the provenance shown to the engineer is false.
evidence: runs/raw/stirling-p1{59,61,63,70}.json; sheet-stats.mts: p159 {pathOps:28, imageCoverage:1, textChars:189} -> 'vector-text', scannerLayer false; p172 {pathOps:0} -> 'scanned'
rootCause: server/drawing/ingest.ts:96-98 hasScannerTextLayer requires pathOps < 20; ingest.ts:87 sends a full-page image with >= 60 text chars to 'scanned' only through that test.
retest: drawing-reader-gaps: invisible / under-image text layer re-OCR'd — confirmed in the final re-measurement

title: Material designation read on 0 of 24 genuine drawings that state one (recall 0/37 material facts); the drawing never answers the material question on any genuine pair
scenario: Extraction scoring (44 truth files) and the 9 costing pairs
expected: Common real-world forms read: 'Material: 5052 H-32 Aluminum', '304 Stainless Steel', '303 SST', '(.1195 THICK) 11 GA 304 SST SHT, ASTM A240', 'Mat: 1.2510', 'Mat: Brass', 'Mat: Steel', '6061' in a GB title block
actual: None read as material.designation. Probe (runs/scripts/probe-material.mts): '5052 H-32 Aluminum' -> [], '304 Stainless Steel' -> [], '303 SST' -> [], '6061' -> [], '6061铝' -> [], 'Brass' -> [], 'Steel' -> [], 'SIS 2541' -> []; '1.2510' only with weak hits allowed, but 'Mat:' is not a recognised label so weak hits are never allowed there. The text WAS read (exact text on SeedMint / OpenEAI; OCR on LulzBot, e.g. '2 Material: 5052 H-32 Aluminum' at 97 %). Consequence: every genuine pair keeps the CAD-only material assumption (POM-C acetal on three aluminium parts, steel DC04 on the 5052 sheet parts); answering the family by hand from the drawing moves the cost +29.7 % to +57.5 % (costing.json Chand).
evidence: runs/extraction.json totals.all.ALL.byGroup.material: correct 0, missed 37; runs/scripts/probe-material.mts; runs/costing.json parts[*].Chand
rootCause: server/drawing/extract/material.ts:144 MATERIAL_LABEL accepts MATERIAL / MAT'L / WERKSTOFF / HALBZEUG but not 'MAT:'; MATERIAL_GRAMMARS (from :22) require AA alloys with a temper written '-H32' / '-T6' (not 'H-32' or bare '6061'), AISI/SAE prefixes for 300-series stainless, and have no trade-name entries (brass, steel, aluminium).
retest: drawing-reader-gaps: material grammar (0 → 94 % / 79 % recall) — confirmed in the final re-measurement

title: Correcting a misread material designation does not re-interpret the material family the reader derived from it: a stale 'steel' stays on the panel as a leaning for the material question
module: server/drawing/extract/material.ts (material.family emitted with no derivedFrom) + src/engine/engineering-data/overrides.ts (correct)
scenario: LulzBot electronics chassis sheet 1: OCR reads '5052' as '30W9'; the reviewer corrects the designation to 5052 (drawingReview correct op); /reanalyze
expected: The family interpreted from '30W9' (steel) is withdrawn and re-interpreted from '5052' (aluminium), as the design states ('correcting a reading re-runs its interpretation')
actual: drawing:material.designation:1 = '5052' status corrected; drawing:material.family:1 = 'steel' (rawText '30W9', 'From the form of the designation "30W9"') still needs-validation and still offered as the leaning for material.family; the corrected '5052' produces no family and answers no question (a careful reviewer has to reject the stale family and answer the family by hand).
evidence: runs/costing-raw/lulzbot-taz6-electronics-chassis@sheet-C-reanalyze.json engineeringData.parameters + drawingCosting.leanings; runs/scripts/manual-review.json (the reject the reviewer had to add)
rootCause: server/drawing/extract/material.ts:180-183 pushes material.family (kind 'interpreted') with no derivedFrom link to the designation; src/engine/engineering-data/overrides.ts:105-117 re-interprets only parameters whose derivedFrom chain reaches the corrected id, so the reader's own family is neither replaced nor reopened (material.condition at :184 has the same shape).
retest: drawing-validation-fixes D04: superseded family on correction — confirmed in the final re-measurement

title: Reports do not say who confirmed or corrected a reading, or when; the correction reason is not printed
module: src/export/drawing-spec-report.ts (DrawingSpecRow) -> core PDF §3, audit pack §9c, workbook 10-Drawing
scenario: Bed plate C costing exported from the screen (runs/exports-c/): 2 corrections, 7 confirmations, 1 conflict settled
expected: The drawing specification table shows each decision's status AND who / when (the history the server stamps: by = signed-in user, at = server clock), and the correction's reason
actual: Rows carry group, parameter, value, source, status ('Corrected' / 'Confirmed'), used — no who, no when, no reason, in all three exports. Only the settled conflict prints 'Settled by qa@test' (no date). The server does hold by/at (engineeringData.parameters[].history).
rootCause: src/export/drawing-spec-report.ts:14-24 — DrawingSpecRow has no by / at / reason fields; buildDrawingSpecReport (:60-77) never reads parameter.history.
retest: drawing-validation-fixes D05: who / when / why in reports — confirmed in the final re-measurement

title: Model revision is never compared with the drawing revision
scenario: SeedMint assembly STEP (PRODUCT 'Base v12', 'Slider v9') with Base Drawing (V10) and Slider Drawing A3 (V22); D2MI 904 (file 'rev c', title block A); LulzBot washer (STEP rev_IR = drawing IR)
expected: The model's revision (STEP product version / file-name revision) set against the title-block revision; a mismatch raised as a conflict or warning
actual: No CAD-side revision parameter on any case; only the drawing's own revision is listed (V10, V22). Nothing flags the mismatch.
rootCause: from-cad.ts emits identity from the STEP product name only (title.partName); no revision is taken from the STEP PRODUCT version string or file name, so reconcile.ts has nothing to compare.
retest: Model revision never compared with the drawing revision

title: A drawing paired with the wrong model is not detected unless hole callouts were read; overall size / thickness are never compared
scenario: (a) nist-ftc-09 drawing on the ftc-10 model; OpenEAI JXS-01-02 drawing on the JXS-05-01 model; also bed-plate drawing on D2MI 906, ftc-10 drawing on CTC-01
expected: Identity, envelope / stock-thickness and feature mismatches flagged
actual: ftc-09 -> ftc-10 and JXS-01-02 -> JXS-05-01: 0 conflicts, 0 callouts without a model feature (FAIL). bed-plate -> D2MI 906: 2 callouts not in the model + a thread-count conflict (PASS, but the part-name conflict also appears with the RIGHT model because the LulzBot STEPs declare 'ASSEMBLY', so it is not a pairing signal). ftc-10 -> CTC-01: 11 callouts 'no hole of Ø… in the 3D model', no identity conflict (PARTIAL). part.envelope from the kernel is never compared with anything; the drawing's stated stock thickness is not read (D03) so the bend-pair gauge is never cross-checked.
rootCause: reconcile.ts compares only hole / thread callouts against the feature table (:174-297) and whole-part names; no drawing overall-size reading exists to set against part.envelope (from-cad.ts:49).
retest: FTC-09 drawing on the FTC-10 model now raises a stock-thickness conflict; OpenEAI pairing still unflagged

title: (CAD-only, pre-existing) A part-number prefix 'PP-' is read as polypropylene and the material family is pre-answered 'plastic' and shown as ANSWERED
scenario: LulzBot bed_plate_v4.5_PP-MP0108.step and corner_bracket_v2.0_PP-MP0106.step, CAD only
expected: No material assumed from a part number; the family question asked (or a name leaning shown, not an answer)
actual: material.family = plastic with source 'answered' in the comparison spec; costed in POM-C acetal stock without any question; the aluminium plate costs £17.30 (bed plate) / £3.50 (bracket). The engineer answered nothing.
evidence: runs/costing.json parts lulzbot-taz6-bed-plate / corner-bracket A.spec = [{material.family: Plastic, answered}]; regression.json: identical at 36f6f7d3
rootCause: src/engine/material-family.ts:20 matches \bpp\b in the file name ('PP-MP0108' -> 'pp mp0108'); server/routes/cad.ts:2192-2205 answersFromContext turns the filename family into answers['material.family'].
retest: drawing-validation-fixes D08: the prefix is matched anywhere in the name — the real LulzBot names (…_PP-MP0108) did not move in the re-measurement; fixed in 90022108

title: (CAD-only, pre-existing) Blank development runs on the server's event loop for ~40 s: the server stops answering, and a client's next request on a kept-alive socket is reset (ECONNRESET)
scenario: LulzBot electronics chassis (1.5 MB STEP, bent sheet) /api/cad/analyze and /reanalyze with the sheet route
expected: Long geometry work off the event loop; other requests (health, other users) served
actual: /api/health took 35.2 s and failed while the chassis was analysed (runs/logs/event-loop-probe.json); 'blank developed from the solid in 39-45 s' in the server log; three runs of the chassis C costing got ECONNRESET on the next /reanalyze until the client retried (costing.json connectionResetsRetried).
evidence: runs/logs/event-loop-probe.json; runs/logs/costing-run3.log; server.log lines '[cad] blank developed from the solid in 42497 ms'
rootCause: server/services/blank-development.ts:58 developed = developBlank(mesh.mesh) — synchronous Tutte/ARAP unfold + forming inverse (server/utils/blank-unfold.ts:605) in the request handler's thread.
retest: Pre-existing: blank development blocks the server event loop ~40 s (deployment risk)

title: (CAD-only, pre-existing) Route leaning contradicts the tool's own plausibility guard on sheet parts
scenario: Electronics chassis (2 mm bent shell): leaning 'machining' -> refused 'thin shell rarely machined from solid'; sheet route on the flat 304 plate ftc-09 (84 % fill) and the electronics cover (99 % fill) -> refused 'near-solid part inconsistent with the thin-wall process'
expected: The leaning is a route the guard accepts; a flat or bent constant-gauge plate is accepted for sheet metal
actual: Chassis cannot be costed on the leaning route; ftc-09 and the cover cannot be costed as sheet metal at all (refused in A and C) — the drawing's stock thickness (2.03 mm, .1195 in) could not help.
evidence: runs/costing.json parts lulzbot-taz6-electronics-chassis (A refused), nist-ftc-09@sheet, lulzbot-taz6-electronics-cover@sheet
rootCause: not traced to a line (out of the drawing feature's scope); the 'near-solid' test uses bounding-box fill, which is high for any flat plate.
retest: Pre-existing: route leaning contradicts the sheet-metal guard

title: Split hole callouts raise false count conflicts: each callout's count is compared with the model's total for that diameter
scenario: nist-ftc-07 (inch drawing, vector) with its STEP
expected: Callouts of the same diameter summed (1 + 2X + 4X + 1 = 8) before comparing with the model's 8 × Ø6.35; no conflict
actual: 4 conflicts the engineer must settle: 'the drawing calls 2 × Ø6.35 and the 3D model has 8 × Ø6.35', '4 × Ø6.35 v 8', '2 × Ø15.0876 v 4 × Ø15.08' (twice). Units are handled correctly (inch converted to mm, exact factor, then matched); the converted value is printed unrounded (Ø15.0876, Ø7.137400000000001 in notes).
rootCause: src/engine/engineering-data/reconcile.ts:218-231 — byCount(atDia, h.count) per callout and flagConflict on countDiffers; no aggregation of callouts sharing a diameter.
retest: FTC-07: 4 false conflicts → 0; FTC-10: one residual (two Ø6 read as dimensions are not summed)

title: Reader attaches flag-note numbers to callouts and truncates a leading digit
scenario: nist-ftc-10 (vector, mm)
expected: '8X Ø2.5 ±0.15' (flag note 4 beside it); general tolerance 'profile 1.5 A B C APPLIES TO ALL UNTOLERANCED SURFACES'
actual: hole.diameter {diameter 2.5, count 8, upper 0.154, lower -0.154} from '8X Ø2.5 ±0.154' (the flag digit became a tolerance digit — a wrong VALUE, status extracted); 'Ø3.5 G6 4'; tolerance.general '.5 A B C APPLIES TO ALL UNTOLERANCED SURFACES' (the '1' lost).
rootCause: not traced to a line; the flag number is a separate text run on the same baseline and is concatenated by line assembly (server/drawing/text-lines.ts).
retest: drawing-reader-gaps: flag-note digits — confirmed in the final re-measurement

title: Shipped accuracy script mislabels a file's content class when the truth's `files` map is keyed by another file name
